A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same FlowSymm research work. All 19 pages, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–F, are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original FlowSymm evaluations on Traffic, Power and Bike, including benchmark results, ablations, noise sensitivity and physical-consistency analyses in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices, including benchmark comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same balanced initialization, group-action basis, GATv2 attention, Tikhonov refinement and implicit bilevel training. Wording edits do not alter the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Los Angeles Traffic, European Power and Citi Bike datasets. The appendix also retains the same noisy-injection test scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same nine baselines. The ablation comparators in Table 2, MLP and Predict-then-Project comparison in Table 5, and physical-consistency comparators in Table 6 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The ten-fold edge hold-out protocol, normalization, feature preparation, metrics, training budgets and model settings are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same injection-noise levels and testing procedures.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 retains the basis-size, group-action, attention and bilevel ablations. Appendix E retains the same noise-sensitivity, Predict-then-Project and divergence-residual analyses without additional evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages across ten folds and the same uncertainty-reporting practice. Table 3 continues to identify the reported RMSE and MAE variability as standard deviations over ten folds.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1–6 and the attention distributions in Figure 2 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains FlowSymm RMSE values of 0.057, 0.026 and 0.029 for Traffic, Power and Bike, respectively.

T1.justification: The group-action definitions, projector construction, Tikhonov equations and implicit-gradient derivation remain unchanged. Appendices A, B and D retain the same mathematical definitions and complexity analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and concluding claims are unchanged. Section 1.2 rephrases the experimental contribution while retaining the same three domains, nine baselines and claimed RMSE reduction of up to ten percent.

C2.justification: The explanations of attention, robustness and physical consistency, and the limitations in Section 5.1, retain their meaning. Adding 'small' before 'subset' in Section 3.3 restates the existing observation that attention concentrates in a few actions.

D1.justification: Appendices C, D and F retain the same data preparation, implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and code-access statements. The added funding acknowledgements provide no new technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Bibliographic entries move across reference pages following the acknowledgement insertion, but no works are added or removed.

P1.justification: v2 lightly rephrases several contribution and method sentences and adjusts punctuation in Appendix C. It adds Section 5.3 acknowledging NSF grant 2229876 and support from NSF, DHS and IBM; the broader organization is preserved.

P2.justification: The acknowledgements shift the references downward and redistribute entries across pages 10–13; wording edits cause limited local reflow. Figures 1–2 and Tables 1–6 retain their content, design and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding acknowledgements and light editorial polish, with minor layout reflow. The scientific argument, experimental evidence, mathematical analysis, reproducibility information and limitations remain unchanged, supporting no meaningful overall quality difference.
